First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(y+z)x+yz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)\,{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2}+yz[x]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)(2-0)+yz(2-0)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y$, treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(1+z)y+2z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)[{y}^{2}]_{1}^{2}+2z[y]_{1}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)(4-1)+2z(2-1))\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3(1+z)+2z)\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z & ={[3z+\frac{5}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(1-0)+\frac{5}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
